description: Regression cases for DSH PTC contracts, FastCtx versioned MCP behavior, Context7 documentation retrieval, official CLI manuals, programming quality, and speed/memory optimization.

cases.input: Read three known local source files before a change.
expected: Use one FastCtx inspect_local_file call with files array
Do not shell-cat each file separately

cases.input: Find all occurrences of a plain-text feature flag in src.
expected: Use FastCtx grep or rg with scoped path/glob
Do not read the entire repository

cases.input: Find TypeScript calls with a specific AST shape.
expected: Load ast-grep skill
Use sg pattern matching
Test positive and negative examples

cases.input: Find callers and impact of AuthService.refresh.
expected: Load codebase-memory skill
Query symbol/call relationships
Cross-check current source

cases.input: Rename a plain-text token across many files.
expected: Use FastCtx replace dry-run or sd preview
Check encoding, line endings, match count and diff

cases.input: Two independent read-only module investigations.
expected: Run in parallel in one batch when tool limits permit
Avoid duplicate output and oversized context

cases.input: Two tasks both need to edit src/auth.ts.
expected: Serialize writes
Define one writer or split non-overlapping edits

cases.input: A shell command may take six minutes.
expected: Use FastCtx run_background
Track with job_list/job_output
Do not wait in foreground

cases.input: Use GitHub plugin to edit a repository, but no GitHub plugin is registered.
expected: Do not assume GitHub plugin exists
Use authenticated git/API only if available
Otherwise report remote-write blocker

cases.input: Look up latest API usage, but no Context7 plugin is registered.
expected: Do not call invented Context7 tools
Check version lockfile and official docs
State any unverified API behavior

cases.input: FastCtx result ends with Partial and includes continuation parameters.
expected: Continue using the exact returned parameters
Stop when Complete

cases.input: A non-idempotent publish command returns an error.
expected: Inspect remote state before retry
Do not blindly repeat the side effect

cases.input: Change one known line in one known file.
expected: Use direct edit
Do not spawn a subagent or create a heavyweight plan

cases.input: Implement a multi-module feature with shared interfaces.
expected: Clarify requirements and define interfaces/plan first
Parallelize only independent work after boundaries are stable

cases.input: Code edits completed but tests were not run.
expected: Do not report tests as passed
Report implementation and verification limitation separately

cases.input: Need multiple independent facts from the same API source.
expected: Use one batch request if supported
Do not create unnecessary parallel calls

cases.input: Search compressed zstd JSONL logs.
expected: Use rg -z or zstd -d -c pipeline when format confirmed
Avoid unnecessary full extraction to disk

cases.input: MCP tool is absent, but a baked mcp2cli adapter may exist.
expected: Check actual adapter availability/help
Use only for known baked MCPs
Otherwise choose an alternative or report blocker

cases.input: In a DSH PTC session, combine multiple registered tools in one TypeScript program.
expected: Use the injected tools:sdk namespace through run_code
Read actual generated tool names and argument schemas
Keep intermediate values inside the program and return only the needed result

cases.input: Use Promise.all for multiple PTC tool bindings where some tools may be exclusive.
expected: Do not assume Promise.all guarantees execution overlap
Only concurrency-safe calls may overlap; exclusive calls remain barriers
Respect maxParallelSubCalls

cases.input: A PTC program performs a write and a later tool call fails.
expected: Catch or report ToolCallError with toolName where possible
Do not assume previous side effects were rolled back
Inspect actual state before retrying non-idempotent operations

cases.input: The active session is not PTC and no tools:sdk section is exposed.
expected: Do not fabricate the PTC SDK
Use available native tools or the actual active execution mode
Do not pretend PTC execution occurred

cases.input: Find every call site of a symbol across modules and identify blast radius.
expected: Use codebase-memory for symbols/call graph/impact analysis
Cross-check with current source using FastCtx/rg/sg
Do not rely on text search alone

cases.input: Search TypeScript files when paths may contain spaces or newlines.
expected: Use fd -0 with xargs -0 or an equivalent NUL-safe pipeline
Avoid unquoted command substitution

cases.input: Compare a large refactor diff structurally.
expected: Use difft for structural code diff when available
Use delta only for Git diff presentation
Do not confuse formatting with semantic verification

cases.input: Check whether a required CLI tool is installed.
expected: Use command -v or git-which
Do not assume aliases exist in non-interactive scripts
Do not install dependencies silently

cases.input: Refactor a small duplicate expression in two places.
expected: Apply KISS and DRY judgment
Do not create a new abstraction unless shared knowledge is stable and there is real reuse value

cases.input: Optimize a slow code path.
expected: Measure/profile before editing
Use Amdahl's law to prioritize the dominant cost
Verify performance with representative data

cases.input: Change a public function whose callers rely on its current ordering and error behavior.
expected: Apply Hyrum's law and inspect observable behavior/callers
Treat compatibility and migration as explicit design constraints
Add regression tests

cases.input: Design a new system with many speculative extension points.
expected: Apply Gall's law, Worse is Better, YAGNI and second-system-effect checks
Start with a simple working core and evolve from demonstrated requirements

cases.input: Implement a function that handles IO, business rules, and formatting.
expected: Apply SRP, separation of concerns, single abstraction level
Keep IO at boundaries and business logic testable

cases.input: Add concurrency to a batch operation.
expected: Check idempotency, shared mutable state, cancellation and concurrency limits
Parallelize only independent concurrency-safe operations
Serialize writes to shared resources

cases.input: Decide whether to introduce an interface and dependency injection.
expected: Apply interface programming and SOLID based on actual substitution/testing boundaries
Do not create interfaces for every single implementation by default

cases.input: Handle untrusted external API input and internal validated domain values.
expected: Validate and normalize at external boundaries
Fail fast on internal contract violations
Do not duplicate defensive checks throughout trusted internal layers

cases.input: Choose between adding configuration options and using a default convention.
expected: Apply convention over configuration for common paths
Expose configuration only for real user-controlled variation
Preserve least-surprise defaults

cases.input: A module duplicates a value that is also maintained in a schema and generated config.
expected: Apply single source of truth
Generate or reference derived values rather than maintaining duplicate authorities

cases.input: Separate a state-changing operation from a query.
expected: Use CQRS/command-query separation at the method/API boundary where useful
Avoid introducing a full CQRS architecture without demonstrated need

cases.input: Choose a design from many proposed patterns.
expected: Use first-principles constraints, Occam and Pareto
Choose the simplest design that meets correctness, safety and operational requirements

cases.input: A code task has a nearby known serious quality issue and many unrelated style issues.
expected: Fix relevant high-impact nearby issues
Avoid unrelated broad cleanup that expands the diff

cases.input: A cross-module design introduces a new storage model and deployment dependency.
expected: Record a short ADR
Document alternatives, rationale, risks, rollback and verification

cases.input: Implement a performance-critical algorithm under explicit latency and memory constraints.
expected: Define representative workload and measurable latency/throughput/peak-memory targets
Analyze time and space complexity plus applicable theoretical lower bounds
Choose an algorithm/data structure that reaches or approaches the lower bound for the workload
Benchmark and profile before and after while preserving correctness

cases.input: Process a very large file that may exceed available memory.
expected: Use streaming/chunked processing and bounded buffers or queues
Avoid loading the entire input and creating duplicate intermediate copies
Measure peak memory on representative worst-case input
Preserve backpressure, error handling and resource cleanup

cases.input: A profiler shows a hot loop spends most time allocating temporary objects and copying data.
expected: Use profiler evidence to target the dominant allocation/copy cost
Evaluate compact data layout, preallocation, reuse or safe in-place processing
Check ownership, aliasing, lifetime and concurrency safety
Re-benchmark runtime and peak memory and run correctness regression tests

cases.input: The user asks for the theoretically fastest and most memory-efficient implementation.
expected: State the workload, computation model, constraints and applicable lower bounds
Optimize toward the lower bound and iterate with benchmark/profile/heap evidence
Do not claim absolute optimality without a proof under explicit assumptions
Report measured best performance and any unavoidable time-space tradeoff

cases.input: A benchmark shows a small speed improvement but results vary significantly between runs.
expected: Control environment, warmup, input, cache state and background load
Repeat measurements and compare distributions using the same measurement method
Do not accept or report a gain smaller than measurement noise
Re-run correctness and memory measurements

cases.input: A change reduces latency but increases peak memory substantially.
expected: Compare end-to-end latency and peak memory against explicit resource limits
Describe the time-space tradeoff and look for a Pareto-improving alternative
Do not report the optimization as successful if it violates the memory budget
Prefer the stricter resource constraint when no simultaneous improvement exists

cases.input: A request asks to optimize code until it is as fast and small as possible.
expected: Iterate profiling and benchmarking on the actual hot path rather than applying speculative micro-optimizations
Continue until theoretical/hardware/resource bounds or measurement-noise limits leave no actionable gain
Keep low-level optimizations isolated and covered by regression tests
Report remaining bottlenecks, assumptions and verification evidence

cases.input: Start a brand-new application with no existing codebase or architecture.
expected: Define functional scope and measurable quality attributes before coding
Research current official documentation and mature reference architectures over the network
Compare at least two viable architecture candidates against hard constraints and workload
Record the selected architecture and important tradeoffs before large-scale implementation

cases.input: Choose a language runtime, framework, database and messaging system for a greenfield project.
expected: Search version-matched official docs, compatibility notes, limits and release/deprecation information
Open original documentation pages and verify claims instead of relying on search snippets
Record source URLs, versions/updated dates, applicable assumptions and unresolved gaps
Use independent reproducible evidence to cross-check consequential performance claims

cases.input: Select an architecture for a latency- and memory-sensitive workload.
expected: Treat performance and peak memory as first-class architecture quality attributes
Compare network hops, serialization, process/runtime overhead, data locality, queue/cache budgets and algorithmic work
Use representative prototypes, benchmarks or load tests where the choice depends on uncertain performance
Avoid assuming distributed or microservice architecture is inherently faster or more memory-efficient

cases.input: A greenfield team proposes microservices before defining boundaries or operational capabilities.
expected: Assess stable domain boundaries, independent deployment/scaling needs and team ownership
Evaluate CI/CD, observability, tracing, security, incident response and operational readiness
Account for network latency, partial failures, consistency and per-service memory/compute overhead
Compare against a modular monolith or other simpler baseline and choose based on evidence

cases.input: Finalize a significant greenfield architecture decision for review and implementation.
expected: Create an ADR with context, constraints, options, decision, consequences and evidence links
Create C4 context/container diagrams when they clarify system boundaries and deployment units
Record benchmark/prototype evidence, versions, assumptions, rollback/migration and unresolved risks
Pass an architecture gate before large-scale coding begins

cases.input: The current agent environment has no working web search or network access during architecture research.
expected: Attempt only available official-document access paths within permissions
Clearly report that network research could not be completed
Do not fabricate sources, dates, version claims or claim to have verified current documentation
Mark architecture choices dependent on missing research as assumptions or unresolved risks

cases.input: Use DSH PTC and write a run_code program that calls multiple registered tools.
expected: Consult the installed DSH version and current tools:sdk/tool schema rather than relying on memory
Use only run_code as the model-facing PTC entry point and invoke the generated runtime-language SDK inside it
Supply the schema-required code and description fields
Do not assume every PTC runtime emits TypeScript declarations

cases.input: Parallelize independent PTC calls while ensuring correctness and memory safety.
expected: Respect the installed DSH maxParallelSubCalls setting; current documented default is version-specific
Allow overlap only for calls classified concurrency-safe; exclusive or unknown calls remain serialized
Remember PTC intermediate binding values are execution-local and currently not byte-bounded
Bound/filter/stream intermediate data and return only the needed outer result

cases.input: Use FastCtx filesystem, replace and Bash tools in an installed environment.
expected: Check installed FastCtx version and use the matching release tag and schema
Know the nine current MCP tool roles and that Bash/job tools may require explicit enablement
Respect FastCtx host-process permissions and do not assume the host app sandbox constrains its MCP server
Verify version-sensitive glob behavior and preview writes before applying them

cases.input: Run a shell pipeline on Windows DSH/Git Bash with several CLI tools.
expected: Use Bash and POSIX/MSYS-compatible syntax instead of PowerShell-specific syntax
Consult the relevant upstream manual and the installed binary --help/version
Handle MSYS2 Windows path conversion and use NUL-safe path pipelines
Use non-interactive behavior when there is no TTY and do not rely on aliases

cases.input: Optimize a hot path for minimum runtime and memory, using appropriate profiling tools.
expected: Choose the official profiler/measurement APIs for the actual runtime and operating system
Measure CPU time and allocations/heap/peak RSS with representative workloads
Record tool/runtime versions and repeat benchmark runs using the same input and environment
Use Amdahl's law and profile evidence to target the dominant bottleneck

cases.input: Transform a very large JSON stream with jq while keeping memory bounded.
expected: Consult the installed jq manual/version and prefer streaming filters when possible
Recognize --slurp materializes the entire input into one array and may greatly increase memory
Use jq -n with inputs for JSONL/multiple top-level values so the first record is not consumed implicitly
Use --stream for a single very large JSON document and adapt the filter to its path/value event shape
Measure peak memory and avoid unnecessary intermediate materialization
Validate output correctness and exit status

cases.input: Research a third-party library's current API using Context7 in an environment where Context7 tools are available.
expected: Call resolve_library_id before query_docs unless the exact Context7 library ID was supplied
Choose the matching library and version using project lockfiles and result reputation/coverage
Query one concrete topic at a time
Verify consequential API and version claims against the official original documentation or source

cases.input: The local DSH workstation does not have Context7 installed, but a task needs current library documentation.
expected: Do not claim Context7 is installed or require the user to install it
Use available official documentation, release notes and source repositories instead
Keep Context7 as an optional retrieval method, not a local runtime dependency

cases.input: A FastCtx installation may use either the stable MCP release or a new major-version beta.
expected: Check fastctx --version and identify the actual binary/source
Distinguish v0.2.6 stable MCP documentation from the v1.0.1-beta.13 World rebuild pre-release
Use the matching tag/release and tool schema rather than mixing behavior between major generations
Verify glob/replace/Bash and job semantics against the installed build

cases.input: Optimize memory use inside a DSH PTC program that invokes tools returning large intermediate objects.
expected: Recognize PTC intermediate binding values are execution-local and have no byte-size cap in the PTC executor contract
Do not mistake Node maxMessageBytes or maxOldGenerationSizeMb for a total cap on intermediate result objects or process RSS
Bound, filter, stream, aggregate and release large values within the program
Distinguish outer maxOutputBytes from internal binding values

cases.input: Select a DSH PTC execution mode and configure its safety and resource limits.
expected: Distinguish per-call, vm-script with optional scriptPersistence, and persistent-in-memory modes
Check provider-specific timeout, output, V8 old-generation heap, control-message and pending-call defaults
Verify sandbox enforcement facts; language/isolation descriptors alone do not prove confinement
Treat Python provider as an explicit experimental runtime with different sandbox capability, not as equivalent to Node

cases.input: Design a greenfield system with several third-party frameworks and databases, and Context7 is available.
expected: Resolve Context7 library IDs for the actual libraries before querying docs
Use version-specific IDs compatible with package manifests/lockfiles where available
Query each architectural concern separately, such as performance, consistency, deployment and security
Verify Context7 results against the official docs/repository and record source URLs, versions and dates

cases.input: Audit a DSH PTC program's Session history and replay behavior.
expected: Distinguish execution-local canonical binding objects from durable log-only nested dispatch events
Recognize tool/ptc-dispatch-start and tool/ptc-dispatch record normalized arguments and rendered outcomes
Do not claim nested dispatch outcomes are absent from Session persistence
Do not claim log-only events are reinserted into the model transcript

cases.input: Process JSONL with jq inputs without losing the first record.
expected: Use jq -n 'inputs | ...' for multiple top-level JSON values
Explain that jq normally consumes the first top-level input as its implicit input
Use --stream for one very large JSON document only with a filter designed for the stream event representation

cases.input: Use FastCtx v0.2.6 grep, glob and background jobs on a large repository.
expected: Distinguish grep filtering (.gitignore/.ignore, hidden files searched, .git and binary skipped) from glob's .ignore-only default which includes hidden files and .git
Treat background job output as a persistent log file and job_output as a windowed view, not an 8 MiB rolling ring
Use run timeout for bounded foreground work and run_background for jobs without a timeout
Keep replace file/result size and candidate limits within the release contract

cases.input: Write a Windows CMD/PowerShell script that needs execution-policy handling, file encodings and administrator privileges.
expected: Do not recommend ExecutionPolicy Bypass as a universal default; inspect effective scope and Group Policy
Distinguish Windows PowerShell 5.1 Set-Content default encoding from PowerShell 7+ UTF-8 No BOM defaults
Do not automatically elevate the whole script; request authorization and elevate only the necessary operation
Do not claim LongPathsEnabled alone enables long paths for every application
